new_statements.quote: [p. 7] Stress and tone are both lexical. Stress goes normally with the high tones. (see phon.) The object pronoun clitics, (see section 3.1.2.2.) the clitic -a (see section 3.2.4.) and the initial vowel of the items below have inherent stress whatever their tonal shape may be. [four items follow: area 'much', eji 'when', ana 'like that', owo 'then', with tone marks] The last three items show functional indications that they could have been noun clauses at some stage. (see section 3.2.) [p. 4] There are two tonal levels in Ekajuk, namely high (H) and low (L) plus a feature of downstep [...] Since tone (like stress) is a feature of the word and all combinations of L H and D are found, compressions of tones are common in one-syllable words. [p. 47] The other object pronouns have all inherent stress and high tone, irrespective of the set which occurs.

new_statements.relation_note: ekaj1238 is not in the catalog and had no existing statements, so this is a new statement rather than a comparison: tone language with a stress statement (stress lexical, normally accompanying high tone). Live sil.org URL answers with an automated-access block (two attempts, both 403); the file was archived copy (Internet Archive, 31 Jul 2024) of the same URL (HTTP 200, 8688016 bytes, 131 pdf pages).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ekajuk is a two-level tone language (H, L, plus automatic downstep, D). Stress is treated as a lexical, word-level property, not a positional one: it normally sits on the high-toned syllable(s) of the word. No initial/penult/final rule is given. A closed set of morphemes (the object-pronoun clitics -m -a -e -r -n, the clitic -a, and the initial vowel of area 'much', eji 'when', ana 'like that', owo 'then') carries inherent stress regardless of its tone. Details are deferred to the separate phonology ('see phon.' = Kleiner & Kleiner 1976, Preliminary phonological statement, microfiche only, not open).
new_statements.exceptions: Object pronoun clitics, the clitic -a, and the initial vowel of area 'much', eji 'when', ana 'like that', owo 'then' have inherent stress whatever their tonal shape; bo '3rd pl.' has its own HD tone pattern and is not in the inherently stressed set.
new_statements.identity_note: Kleiner & Kleiner 1968 describe the Ekajuk of Ntunop village (about 25 miles south of Ogoja) with assistants from Ntunop, Bansara and one other village, fieldwork April 1966 - July 1967; they state there is little diversity of speech within the Ekajuk clan (ms p. 1). Blench treats Ekajuk as one of the Bakor (Nkum sub-group) lects of Ekoid.
